dossier.public_summary: The dip looks deep and flat-bottomed but only appears as three transits with very different depths and at two different depths in two sectors. Odd and even dips also differ strongly and the transit is too long for the small M-dwarf, all of which matches a grazing eclipsing binary at twice the period rather than a 3.6-Earth-radius planet. The signal is not consistent with a stable planet transit.

reasons.why: Depth is 88.1% different between sectors (7546 +/-1607 ppm in sector 46 vs 19428 +/-1671 ppm in sector 91). sector_depths_by_source says changes_within_a_source, so it is a true change, not a pipeline calibration difference.
With only 3 transits total, depths are inconsistent at p~3.3e-06, so the signal is not persistently repeated at the same depth — a few bad/ blended events would produce this.

Duration 2.999h vs central 1.88h is too long for a central transit on this 0.28 Rsun M dwarf, and the transit shape does not match the stellar density, favouring a grazing eclipsing binary or diluted blended EB over a planet.
Odd and even depths differ by factor ~1.9 at 3.405 sigma, consistent with an EB at twice the period (period_x2 25.4d) with unequal eclipses, not a planet with equal transits.
Independent classifier trained on follow-up outcomes ranks this in the false-positive/low-planet region, consistent with the depth-instability and odd/even evidence.
